text: Git branching is a key part of modern version control workflows. When developers work on a new feature, they usually create a feature branch instead of changing the main code directly. This keeps the main branch stable while new work is tested safely. Once the feature is finished, the team merges the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, developers often open a pull request so others can review the code, leave comments, and suggest improvements. This simple workflow helps teams collaborate, avoid conflicts, and keep track of every change made to a project over time.
